subject: open-interpreter
title: Whole transport plane reshapes the codex engine into 14 rival coding-agent contracts (system prompt, tool specs, wire format, SSE parsing, compaction prompts) to match what low-cost models were tuned on
evidence: core/src/harness/routing.rs:14-44 (StreamTransportRoute enum: ChatHarness route per rival, ClaudeCode over Responses/Chat variants); core/src/harness/ (20,072 LOC rs, 155+ inline tests incl. claude_code.rs:2504, kimi_cli.rs:1418, routing.rs:186); core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:1045-1075 (alias Bash/Read/Edit tools re-dispatched to native policy-bound handlers); README.md:47 product thesis ('emulating the agent harness that gets the best performance out of low-cost models'); docs/config.md:154-166
one_why: Distinct from the study's existing spoof cluster (oauth-client-impersonation: claurst/qqcode borrow a vendor IDENTITY to pass subscription gates) - here the unit of borrowing is the agent CONTRACT: prompt+tool+wire transcribed per rival harness so cheap models behave as they were benchmarked, while approvals/sandbox stay codex-native. No other subject shapes one engine into 14 rival client surfaces; the per-harness compaction-prompt rewriting is the subtlest piece.

subject: open-interpreter
title: Rival agents' system prompts and compaction prompts reproduced near-verbatim inside an Apache-2.0 repo
evidence: core/src/harness/claude_code_prompt.rs:5-32 (Claude Code system prompt incl. '/help ... report the issue at https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues'); core/src/harness/kimi_code_system_prompt.md:1 and kimi_cli_prompt.md:1 ('You are Kimi Code CLI...'); core/src/harness/zcode.rs:41 (full ZCode compaction prompt); opencode_system_prompt.md / opencode_search_agent_prompt.md
one_why: Convergence with claw-code-agent-2: prompts are expressive copyrighted text; here the exposure is structural - ~6 rival prompt corpora are a load-bearing product feature (harness mode), so takedown-style pressure would hit functionality, not just strings. Apache compliance vs upstream Codex (open-interpreter-1) does not cover third-party prompt assets.

subject: open-interpreter
title: Harness modes ship rival client identity headers ('claude-cli/2.1.158 (external, sdk-cli)', 'Bun/1.3.14', ZCode referer/user-agent) with no fork-owned header on the wire
evidence: core/src/harness/claude_code.rs:52-53,131-136 (UA + beta headers, ANTHROPIC beta constants); core/src/harness/zcode.rs (ZCODE_USER_AGENT/ZCODE_REFERER/ZCODE_VERSION consts); core/src/client.rs:1178,2470 (routes select these headers)
one_why: Lighter sibling of claurst-2/qqcode-3: no OAuth-token-stealing or billing-salt machinery observed - the spoofed identity rides user-supplied provider keys - but requests to vendor-shaped endpoints present zero Open Interpreter identity, which is ToS-visible impersonation and the one surface where FORK_BRANDING.md's honesty policy does not reach the wire.

subject: open-interpreter
title: Persistent cron scheduler in-process: disk-persisted tasks, coalesced missed fires, jittered fire times, same-thread <cron-fire> envelope injection
evidence: core/src/kimi_cron.rs:225-365 (run_scheduler, load_from_disk, persist_task, remove_persisted_task), :390 count_coalesced, :411 jittered_fire_time; core/src/kimi_cron_tests.rs (envelope render + one-shot due-time tests); tools/handlers/kimi_code_cron.rs
one_why: Convergence (scheduled-agent-runs, previously x4): the stealable bits are the missed-fire coalescing count and jitter (a fleet of restarted sessions must not thundering-herd the provider) and delivering the fire as a structured contextual fragment into the same thread rather than spawning a new run; test coverage thin (2 tests) for the crash-recovery path.

subject: open-interpreter
title: External-agent session import with sha256-content idempotency ledger - convert rival transcripts to rollout items, never double-import
evidence: codex-rs/external-agent-sessions/src/detect.rs:16-105 (detect_recent_sessions + save_import_ledger); export.rs load_session_for_import_with_content_sha256; ledger.rs CompletedExternalAgentSessionImport / has_current_session_been_imported; 2,194 LOC crate with inline tests
one_why: Convergence with cline-b1 (rival-harness-session-import) - second independent subject to build it; the ledger keyed on content sha256 is the nuance cline lacks, making re-scans of ~/.config cheap and re-import-safe, which is what makes the feature shippable as a startup prompt instead of a one-shot command.
